items.text: Remove spaces inserted between CJK characters in transcript output

comments.text: Closed via commit 9bebc5d. Root cause: helpers.py:381 unconditionally appended `wrd + " "` after every word. Fix: added _is_cjk + _append_word helpers, CJK-aware join. Regression test: tests/test_helpers.py (26 cases). Full suite 97/97 green.

meta.originalText: remove spaces from transcript containing CJK characters. Currently, obtained transcript using server.py have spaces between CJK characters (e.g. Chinese, Japanese)

items.description:
**Problem:** Transcripts produced via `server.py` contain spurious spaces between CJK characters (e.g. Chinese, Japanese).
**Expected:** CJK characters in the transcript should appear without inserted spaces.
**Actual:** Obtained transcripts currently have spaces inserted between CJK characters.
**Context:** Reproducible via `server.py` transcript output.

items.text: Latin words over-spaced in CJK transcripts

comments.text: use whisper conda env when fixing.

Closed via fix commit. Root cause: bug-1's _append_word ignored Whisper's leading-space word-boundary marker, inserting a space between every pair of non-CJK tokens. Fix: _append_word now treats leading-space tokens as new words (one separator, suppressed at CJK boundaries) and bare tokens as continuations (append directly). Regression test: tests/test_helpers.py (3 new bug-2 cases + 2 bug-1 cases updated for realistic token shapes). Full suite 102/102 green.

meta.originalText: for transcripts containing both CJK and latin characters (e.g. predominantly Chinese but also has english words and phrases), CJK character space is fixed by bug-1, but English words are spaced two spaces apart, and each latin character is spaced one space apart (e.g. if I speak "你好世界的英文是Hello world", the output will be "你好世界的英文是H e l l o  w o r l d"). Expected: latin languages properly spaced in CJK sentences (expected output should be "你好世界的英文是Hello world")

items.description:
**Problem:** Transcripts mixing CJK and Latin text render Latin words with characters separated by single spaces and words separated by double spaces.
**Expected:** Latin languages properly spaced in CJK sentences (e.g. "你好世界的英文是Hello world").
**Actual:** Output is "你好世界的英文是H e l l o  w o r l d" — each Latin character spaced one apart, words two apart.
